title: IT Project Manager — Budget, Risk & EVM

companyIntro.name: Nimbus Digital
companyIntro.mission: Ship reliable software for mid-market clients without the chaos of ad-hoc project management.
companyIntro.culture: Sprint-disciplined and blameless-retro focused. People here are expected to raise blockers loudly and early.

projectBackground.name: Meridian Client Portal Rebuild
projectBackground.context: The portal is behind schedule and over budget. The sponsor wants a forecast and a recovery plan.

manager.name: Julia Hoffmann
manager.note: Don't tell me it's amber. Tell me how far behind, how much over and what you'll do about it.

assignment.title: Forecast and recover the portal project
assignment.brief: Compute CPI and EAC, analyse three work packages in Excel, choose risk responses and write the steering committee update.

documents.name: Project Status
documents.note: Planned value €400,000; earned value €360,000; actual cost €450,000.

documents.name: Work Package Data
documents.note: Three packages with PV, EV and AC.

tasks.title: Cost Performance Index
tasks.prompt: EV is €360,000 and AC is €450,000. What is CPI?
tasks.mistake: Dividing AC by EV inverts the meaning.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Estimate at Completion
tasks.prompt: BAC is €1,000,000 and CPI is 0.8. Assuming current efficiency continues, what is EAC (€)?
tasks.reasoning: If performance continues, the final cost is BAC divided by CPI.
tasks.mistake: Adding the overrun to BAC assumes recovery of efficiency.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Risk Response
tasks.prompt: A key integration vendor may deliver late. Which is a mitigation?
options: Agree an early-delivery milestone and prepare a fallback integration
tasks.reasoning: Mitigation reduces probability or impact before the risk occurs.
tasks.tip: Assign an owner and a trigger.
tasks.mistake: Passive acceptance without a plan is not a response.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Recovery Options
options: Ask the team to work unpaid overtime indefinitely
Add a time-boxed spike to resolve the integration risk
tasks.reasoning: Recovery needs transparency, scope control and risk reduction.
tasks.mistake: Burn-out and hiding variance destroy trust.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: EVM by Work Package (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Calculate CPI (E = C / D) and SPI (F = C / B) for each work package and upload.
tasks.reasoning: Work-package EVM shows where the project is actually in trouble: Integration.
tasks.tip: Look for the worst package, not the average.
tasks.mistake: Reporting only project-level CPI hides the problem area.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Steering Update
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence update to the steering committee.
tasks.modelAnswer: The project is 10% behind schedule (SPI 0.9) and 20% over cost (CPI 0.8). If efficiency continues, the forecast cost is €1.25M against a €1.0M budget. The main driver is the Integration package (CPI 0.67, SPI 0.8). We propose de-scoping two low-value features and a time-boxed spike with the vendor to resolve the integration risk. We ask the committee to approve the revised plan and decide by Friday.
tasks.reasoning: A good update states variance, forecast, cause, plan and the decision needed.
tasks.mistake: Colour ratings alone don't help decisions.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Green Project That Wasn't
caseStudy.background: A project reported green for six months using task-completion percentages. EVM later showed CPI 0.7; the overrun was found when the budget ran out.
caseStudy.challenges: Status was reported by tasks done, not value earned.
caseStudy.constraints: No cost data in status reports.
caseStudy.solution: Nimbus required CPI, SPI and EAC in every status report.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Measure value earned against cost, not activity.

prompts: How do you tell a sponsor bad news?
